text:
nina: Hey team — running the Go quickstart in CI and the very first POST to /v1/chat returns 403 "billing: payg_disabled" even though the org shows billing enabled in the console. anyone seen this?

nina: logs: `caller=auth status=200 token_ok` then `caller=provision status=403 msg="billing: payg_disabled org_lookup_failed"`

harry: are you using a user token, service account, or OIDC from the runner? which quickstart image?

nina: service account token mounted into the container by CI (no email or user claim). quickstart: starter-go v0.7.

maya: this matches other onboarding hits — provisioning service needs an org mapping (email or org claim). service-account/CI tokens often lack that so the payg check returns workspace_unprovisioned / payg_disabled.

maya: short term workaround: send x-redwood-org with the org id. example: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-redwood-org: org_07ZYY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-mini","input":"hi"}'`

nina: confirmed — after adding x-redwood-org header the starter app returns 200 and the stream starts. saved my morning. :thumbsup:

harry: filing INF-5000 to add REDWOOD_ORG env support in quickstart images, a snippet in the README, and a small SDK helper to set the header for container examples. also request changing the error to a clearer code "missing_org_mapping" so DX can act on it.

devex-bot: note: payg-guard v1.3.3 rolled out 2026-03-23T10:00:00Z — tightened identity-to-org checks.

sdk-bot: reminder: Node and Python SDKs currently return different shapes for auth/billing failures; parity ticket INF-5001 created.

nina: thanks all — will use header as a stopgap and watch for the quickstart update.
